findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Either tag AC #4 `[operator-attested]` with a concrete pre/post screenshot attached to the ticket, or add an automated tally-identity check (e.g. capture `pytest --tb=no -q | tail -1` before and after, assert the summary line is identical) and include it as the proving command.
evidence: "The gold-set score tally is identical to the pre-change baseline (recorded in a ticket comment before the edit, compared after)."

The pytest invocation `pytest tests/unit/gold_set_completion.py tests/unit -k 'eval or gold'` passes even if the tally shifts, because the tests assert correctness of the new vocabulary, not identity of the tally count.
The criterion does not carry the `[operator-attested]` tag.
findings.finding: AC #4 requires proving that the gold-set score tally is IDENTICAL to the pre-change baseline, but the only stated proving mechanism is a manual comparison ('recorded in a ticket comment before the edit, compared after'). There is no automated command that would fail if the tally diverged, and the criterion is not tagged `[operator-attested]`, so an executor has no deterministic in-session check.
scenarios: An executor edits an expectation string that inadvertently changes a pass to a fail (or vice versa), the pytest run is still green because the expectation is now internally consistent, but the tally has shifted — AC #4 is violated with no automated signal.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Testing section, add: `before=$(pytest tests/unit/gold_set_completion.py --tb=no -q 2>&1 | tail -1); # make edits; after=$(pytest tests/unit/gold_set_completion.py --tb=no -q 2>&1 | tail -1); [ "$before" = "$after" ] && echo TALLY_UNCHANGED`. This gives an unambiguous in-session binary check.

findings.finding: The plan-review-g7.eval.yaml gold_set references three case IDs (G7-R-redefines-parent-deliverable, G7-P-partial-of-parent, G7-P-subset-scope) that have no corresponding dataset: entries in the same file. These are orphaned gold labels — the LLM judge is calibrated against descriptions of scenarios that are never presented to the model as eval cases. The plan's scope for this file is only ':36' (the rubric text) and does not address these orphaned labels. If the judge kappa computation over this gold_set exercises these entries, the 'tally unchanged' AC is measuring against a structurally incomplete corpus, making the vocabulary-only claim unverifiable for those three labels.
scenarios: The 'gold-set score tally unchanged' AC (AC line 4) runs the judge against all gold_set entries including the three orphaned ones; since no model output corresponds to these entries, the kappa/tally computation is vacuous for them, making the baseline comparison misleading.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a sentence to the Approach explaining why changing 'success criteria' → 'acceptance criteria' in dataset input strings (container.eval.yaml:91,93) is semantically neutral for LLM-judged scorers (e.g., because deterministic scorers gate the build and LLM-judge variance is absorbed by the epoch/gate setting, or because the semantic meaning of the scenario is unchanged).
evidence: Plan states edits are 'straight vocabulary edits' without distinguishing rubric text from model-visible dataset input strings.
container.eval.yaml:91 input string 'An epic whose success criteria include …' is fed to an LLM in the eval run; changing it changes model input, not just a label or constant.
The LLM-judge scorer (container_finding_grounded_against_roster) uses model output over this exact input — vocabulary shift in input can in principle shift output.
No rationale is given for why the LLM scorer outcome is insensitive to this change (e.g., because the deterministic gate dominates, or epochs/gate absorb variance).
findings.finding: The plan does not provide a positive rationale for why editing the dataset *input* strings in `plan-review-container.eval.yaml` (lines 91, 93) — text shown directly to the LLM during eval — is semantically neutral and will not shift LLM-judged scorer output. These are fixture scenario strings (natural language describing a ticket's content), not rubric or spec vocabulary; the plan groups them with rubric edits without explaining the distinction or why the LLM scorer is insensitive to this vocabulary swap.
scenarios: An implementer changes the dataset input text and the LLM-judge scorer produces different output across epochs, shifting the tally — the 'identical tally' AC fails and the reason is unclear.
A reviewer asks why dataset scenario prose (not rubric text) needed to change, finds no rationale, and incorrectly reverts the change.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Approach section, after 'Specs and gold-set strings are straight vocabulary edits,' add: 'The dataset input strings at container.eval.yaml:91,93 are also updated; these are LLM-visible scenario prose, but the scenario semantics are unchanged (an idempotency criterion still has no covering child), so deterministic scorer outcomes are unaffected. LLM-judge variance across these inputs is bounded by the 3-epoch / at_least(2) gate, which the tally AC verifies.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a fallback protocol to the Testing section specifying what to do if the gold-set tally shifts after editing expectation strings (e.g. acceptable tolerance, human adjudication step, or revert criterion).
evidence: Testing section: 'Confirm the gold-set pass/fail tallies are UNCHANGED versus the pre-change baseline, proving the edits were vocabulary-only and did not move any expectation.'
AC: '- [ ] The gold-set score tally is identical to the pre-change baseline (recorded in a ticket comment before the edit, compared after).'

findings.finding: The Testing section requires 'confirm the gold-set pass/fail tallies are UNCHANGED versus the pre-change baseline' but specifies no fallback or resolution protocol if the tallies do shift. Expectation strings fed to the LLM judge are semantically equivalent but not lexically identical after editing (e.g. 'success criteria could be sized' → new wording); the judge may score the rephrased strings differently, causing a tally change. The plan provides no guidance on whether a tally shift means revert, iterate, or accept with a tolerance band.
findings.location: Plan Testing section / AC line 4 ('The gold-set score tally is identical to the pre-change baseline')
scenarios: An LLM judge scores 'del-b's acceptance criteria could be sized into two tasks' differently from 'del-b's success criteria could be sized into two tasks' due to prompt sensitivity, causing a tally mismatch that blocks the AC but has no prescribed resolution.
An executor is left guessing whether to revert the expectation string, accept the delta, or debug the judge.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Testing: 'If tallies shift by more than N cases, treat as a non-vocabulary change: inspect the differing cases, adjudicate whether the judge is behaving correctly on the new wording, and either accept (with a ticket comment documenting the delta) or revert the expectation string to preserve the original tally.'
